thought: A duty cut wiped out his factory. His bank reportedly took his house. He rebuilt into a company worth over Rs 12,000 crore.
support: In the early 1990s, a sudden cut in import duties collapsed Rajat Agrawal's family lead-recycling business - reportedly costing him his home too, by his own account retold in later profiles. Instead of quitting, he moved the operation to Sri Lanka, then Africa. That venture became Gravita India, now worth over Rs 12,000 crore after a 2024 fundraise from Goldman Sachs and Mirae Asset.
